data.long_meaning: Derived from the Hebrew name Shimon, which means 'he who hears.' In the New Testament, Simon Peter is a disciple of Jesus who is given this name by Jesus. The name Simonea carries the meaning “God hears” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew, Greek. Parents who choose Simonea usually hope their child will grow to embody god hears and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.etymology: Simonea belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “God hears.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Simonea total 4, giving a life-path number of 4. Number 4 is linked with Rahu and with the qualities of stability, discipline and hard work.

in_hebrew.name: שמעונאה
in_hebrew.long_meaning: השם שמעונאה הוא נגזר מהשם העברי שמעון שפירושו שמעה אלוהים. השם שמעונאה הוא שינוי נקבה של השם שמעון ומשמעותו היא שמעה אלוהים, האלה שמעה אלוהים. השם נמצא בשימוש בקרב קהילות יהודיות ונוצריות כאחד.

in_greek.name: Σιμωνέα
in_greek.long_meaning: Το όνομα Σιμωνέα προέρχεται από το εβραϊκό όνομα Σίμων, που σημαίνει ακούω τον Θεό. Η Σιμωνέα είναι η θηλυκή μορφή του ονόματος Σίμων και σημαίνει αυτή που ακούει τον Θεό. Το όνομα αυτό απαντάται στην Καινή Διαθήκη και ήταν δημοφιλές στην αρχαία Εκκλησία.

in_latin.name: Simonea
in_latin.long_meaning: The name Simonea is derived from the Hebrew name Simeon, which means 'he who hears'. The feminine form Simonea signifies she who hears God. This name has been used in Christian tradition and symbolizes a deep spiritual connection with the divine.

in_english.name: Simonea
in_english.meaning: She who hears God, listener of divine messages
in_english.long_meaning: The name Simonea originates from the Hebrew name Simeon, meaning 'he who hears'. Its feminine form, Simonea, translates to 'she who hears God'. This name is rooted in biblical etymology and signifies a person with a strong spiritual inclination, attentive to divine guidance. Historically, the name has been used in Christian tradition, symbolizing a deep connection with faith.

data.cultural_impact: The name Simonea, with its origin in both the Hebrew and the Latin cultures, has a unique charm and a rich history. In the Hebrew culture, it is derived from the name Shimon which is commonly used among Jews. In the Latin culture, it is derived from the name Simon or Simone, which was popular in the Roman Empire. The name gained popularity in European countries, including Romania, where it is still used today.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Simonea carries a deep spiritual meaning as it was bestowed upon a disciple of Jesus, Simon Peter. According to the New Testament, Jesus changed Simon's name to Peter, which means 'rock.' Peter became a leader among the apostles and is considered the first Pope in the Catholic Church. Thus, the name Simonea represents a strong spiritual foundation and a connection to the faith and teachings of Jesus Christ. It suggests resilience, steadfastness, and a deep commitment to following the word of God.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Simonea: Dedicated to the divine mother, bearing the strength and nurturing love of the Virgin Mary. Embracing grace and wisdom from the Divine Feminine.

historical_references.reference: Simonea, the mother of St. John the Apostle, is mentioned in the New Testament book of John (21:7) as being present when her son and the other disciples went fishing after Jesus' resurrection.

Simone Stylites (c. 459-543 AD) was a Syrian ascetic, who lived on a pillar for several decades as a form of penance and devotion. Her name 'Simone' is a variant of the New Testament character's name 'Simon Peter's mother'.
